{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study systematically compares the overlap between diseases investigated by GWAS and those investigated in pharmaceutical R&D, quantifying the extent to which these efforts align. It reports quantitative measures like percentages of diseases covered by each effort and their overlap, fulfilling the inclusion criteria.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "The study systematically maps drug development and genomic discovery efforts in common diseases to produce target-disease indication lists. These lists could help the pharmaceutical industry to prioritize future drug development efforts based on genetic evidence, academia to prioritize future GWAS for diseases without effective treatments, and both sectors to harness genetic evidence to expand the indications for licensed drugs or to identify repurposing opportunities for clinical candidates that failed in their originally intended indication.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study analyzes disease coverage across a broad range of human diseases investigated by GWAS and pharmaceutical R&D, rather than focusing on a single therapeutic area. It aims to understand the overlap and divergence of these efforts across the entire 'disease-ome'.",
  "model_type": "regulatory-dataset",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes data from large-scale public databases (ChEMBL, GWAS Catalog, UK Biobank) and compares findings across these datasets, akin to analyzing regulatory or large-scale observational datasets for concordance.",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study focuses on human diseases and human genetic studies (GWAS) and drug development, without analyzing specific animal models or species.",
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study discusses both disease endpoints (e.g., 'treatment of a specific disease/diagnosis') and biomarkers (e.g., 'validated clinical biomarker (e.g., LDL cholesterol for coronary heart disease)'), and the overlap between them in drug development and GWAS."
}
